_what: Personal Calendar tasks are rows in the generic Lists owner. Each row carries a title, description, priority, labels, duration, due date, scheduled interval, optional repeat rule, source identity and completion status. Calendar reads and changes the same rows other list screens and tools see.

list.label: Calendar tasks
list.about: Tasks you can schedule on your calendar.

collections.label: Task lists
collections.about: Named lists that organize Calendar tasks: a colour, a default calendar, an archive flag, their place in the order, whether the planner places their tasks and the times it prefers for them.

day_hours.label: Day hours
day_hours.about: One-day changes to your working hours: start later, stop early, block hours or take the whole day off. The planner subtracts them; your standing hours stay as they are.

working_hours.label: Working hours
working_hours.about: When you work, in your own time zone, and what a sender is told when they write to you outside it (quiet-hours.json modes). One row.

fields.label: When someone writes outside these hours
Move planned tasks out of the way of a task I move
Put planned tasks on my calendar
Who sees my planned tasks on my calendar
Sort emails into Email, Calendar and Other

meeting_filters._what: Which calendar events a person is offered to pull into their tasks (action from_event). A row is a test on one field of the event: `is` (a value or a list), `at_most`, `more_than`, or `matches` (a pattern). An event any active row matches is refused with that row's id. `default` rows are active unless the caller names its own `filters`. An event with no value for the row's field is never matched by it. Add a test by adding a row.

from_source._what: A task made for a thing a person works from (a message, a document), found again by its source id (action from_source; find_source reads without making one). `default_minutes` is its length until the person sets one.

preferences._what: Planning choices a person can flip, stored on the working-hours row. A row with `choices` takes one of them (external_display: whether planned tasks are also put on the person's own calendar as events, and how they show to others; `off` writes nothing, which is what a person who never chose gets; the rows are parts/ui/show/schedule-calendar/timebox-policy.json). `refit_on_move`: when a person moves or schedules a task over tasks the planner placed (and that are not pinned), those tasks are taken off the calendar and wait in the tasks, with one undo for the lot. The default here is what a person who never chose gets. `ai_scheduling`: whether the planner places tasks for the person at all. `default_todo_visibility`: who sees a planned task put on their calendar (private, or visible like any event). `email_todos`: whether the inbox is turned into todos; `email_split_contents`: whether those are sorted into Email, Calendar and Other (email_split); `email_todo_account`: which mail account (empty means every connected one). A row with kind `text` takes a string of at most `most_chars`; empty clears it.

email_split._what: Which built-in list a message becomes a todo in (smart_list on the task). The first row whose test matches the message wins; a row with no test is the default. A test is one message fact (`subject`, `from`, `labels`, `list_unsubscribe`, `has_invite`) with `is` (a value, or a list of values; for `labels` any label), `contains` (text, any case) or `matches` (a pattern). Add a rule by adding a row before the default.

undo._what: Every change to Calendar tasks answers with `undo`, the one action (restore) that puts the changed fields back, if no one has changed them since. These fields belong to a repeating series or to the order of the list and are never restored by it; a change that touched one answers no undo.

bulk._what: One small repair to many tasks at once (action `bulk`, with `task_ids` and a `repair` id). Each repair is a row here: `change` is exactly the single-task change input it applies to every chosen task (so it passes the same checks and leaves the same undo), so a new repair is a new row. One undo takes back all that changed; a task that could not take the change is listed with the reason and the others still change.

rollover._what: Carrying unfinished work forward: a task whose scheduled time is on an earlier day than `today` (in the person's time zone) loses that block and goes back to the unscheduled pool for the planner; a task whose date-only due is earlier than `today` is due `today`. A due with a time of day, a repeating task and a finished task are left alone, with the reason.

words.bad_capacity: Give the most minutes of planned work a day (1 to 1440), a caution band, and weekday limits from 0 (Sunday) to 6.
words.bad_bulk: Choose a repair and the tasks to apply it to.
words.bad_duration: Duration must be a whole number of minutes from 1 to 1440.
words.bad_due: Due must be a date or a date and time.
words.bad_description: Description must be 10000 characters or fewer.
words.bad_priority: Choose low, medium, high or super priority, or leave it blank.
words.bad_labels: Use up to 20 non-empty labels, each 80 characters or fewer.
words.bad_start: Start must be a valid date and time.
words.bad_minimum_duration: The smallest useful slice is a whole number of minutes, at least 5 and shorter than the task.
words.bad_slices: Slices are two or more times that start in order and do not overlap.
words.bad_deadline_type: Choose a deadline kind from the list, or leave it blank.
words.bad_start_on: Start no earlier than must be a date or a date and time.
words.bad_pinned_until: Pinned until must be a date or a date and time.
words.bad_blocked_by: Choose other Calendar tasks to wait for, each once and no more than the limit.
words.bad_placed_by: Placed by must name who placed the task.
words.bad_restore: Restore needs tasks and the fields to put back, as they were and as they are now.
words.restore_changed: A task changed since. Nothing was put back.
words.bad_rollover: Rollover needs today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the person's time zone, like America/New_York.
words.rollover_too_many: There are more open tasks than one rollover reads. Name the tasks to carry.
words.bad_day_hours: Day hours need a day (YYYY-MM-DD) and at least one of: off, a start, an end or blocked hours, in whole minutes of the day.
words.bad_working_hours: Working hours need a start and end like 09:00, a time zone like America/New_York, working days from 0 (Sunday) to 6, and a mode from the list.
words.bad_zone_drift: Zone drift needs the device's time zone, like America/New_York, and whether to move plans to it.
words.bad_event: An event to pull in needs an id, a source, a title and a start and end that come in order.
words.bad_source: A task for something you work from needs its source id and a title.
words.bad_filters: Filters name rows of the meeting filter list.
words.bad_preference: Choose a planning preference from the list and set it to true or false.
words.bad_task: That task is not in your Calendar tasks.
words.bad_parent: That parent task is not in your Calendar tasks.
words.bad_collection: Give the list a name of 200 characters or fewer.
words.bad_collection_field: That list setting is not valid: choose a colour from the list, a calendar, a yes or no, or times from 0 to 1440 minutes with the end after the start.
words.bad_message: A message to turn into a todo needs an id.
words.bad_messages: Give up to 50 messages, each with an id.
words.bad_snoozed_until: Snoozed until must be a date or a date and time.
words.bad_reminder_at: Reminder must be a date and time.
words.bad_time_spent: Time spent is a whole number of minutes from 0 to 100000, and a time log adds 1 to 1440.
words.bad_smart_list: Choose Email, Calendar or Other, or leave it blank.
words.bad_collection_order: Choose a list to move and the list to put it before or after.
words.bad_key: A request key is required so retrying does not make the task twice.
